headline: Corn ends the week at $4.47¾; crude up 2.1% to $104.12
lead: December corn settled Friday at $4.47¾, down 3½ cents, its second lower close in a row, while beans held near $12.22. Corn is giving ground with harvest running and soybeans steady, so the feed side of the ledger got cheaper this week.
teaser: Corn slipped to $4.47¾ Friday while crude ran up to $104.12; cattle and hogs ended the week lower.

one_number.unit: Nov '27 beans to Dec '27 corn ratio
one_number.context: The ratio uses next year's contracts, so it is the one to watch for 2027 acres. At 2.48, the new-crop price signal sits close to even between the two crops.

sections.title: Grains end the week soft
sections.body:
- December corn settled at **$4.47¾**, down 3½ cents, while November soybeans added 2½ cents to $12.22¼.
- Wheat finished at $6.03½, barely changed, and AgWeb's Gulke called the grain markets in free fall.
sections.so_what: Corn is sliding while beans hold steady.

sections.title: Cattle and hogs slip
sections.body:
- December hogs settled at **$58.88**, down 1.6%, near the bottom of their 52-week range.
- October live cattle fell 2.4% to $220.95 and November feeders dropped 2.5% to $337.78, and AgWeb asked if the drop is more than a healthy correction.

sections.title: Crude stays high
sections.body:
- WTI crude was last at **$104.12**, up 2.1%, in Friday afternoon trading; that is a last trade, not a settle.
- Agri-Pulse reported states were asked to waive dyed diesel restrictions, and Chevron said profits nearly tripled to $9.9 billion on strong refining.
sections.so_what: Fuel costs stay a story while crude holds over $100.

outside_the_pit.title: Senate farm bill scores $4.4 billion; lame-duck passage uncertain
outside_the_pit.body: AgWeb reports the Senate farm bill now has a $4.4 billion score. Passage in the lame-duck session after the election is not certain.

watch_list.desc: USDA Crop Progress. Harvest pace shows how much supply is still coming.
Export sales. Weak soybean numbers would sit awkwardly beside steady bean futures near $12.
Crude holding above $100 keeps diesel and input costs in the news.

source_summary: CME Group settlements, USDA, AgWeb, Agri-Pulse, Feedstuffs, oilprice.com

facts.sentence: On Friday, Oct 30, 1,677 of the 1,778 elevators AGSIST reads posted a lower cash corn bid than Thursday, 84 a higher one; 160 changed their basis, 39 weaker and 121 stronger.
facts.detail: 17 unchanged; median change 3¢ lower. Biggest state move: Iowa, 3¢ lower (392 elevators).
facts.unit: cents per bushel, median change in cash bid
facts.source: AGSIST elevator network, last posted bid per trading day (data/bids-prev)

facts.sentence: On Friday, Oct 30, 1,164 of the 1,538 elevators AGSIST reads posted a lower cash soybean bid than Thursday, 292 a higher one; 415 changed their basis, 350 weaker and 65 stronger.
facts.detail: 82 unchanged; median change 1¢ lower. Biggest state move: Nebraska, 3¢ lower (184 elevators).
facts.unit: cents per bushel, median change in cash bid
facts.source: AGSIST elevator network, last posted bid per trading day (data/bids-prev)

facts.sentence: Corn basis on Nov 1 ran from 55¢ over December futures in Texas to 90¢ under in North Dakota, state medians of the elevators AGSIST read at 4:17 a.m. CT.
facts.detail: Elevators behind each median: Texas 17, North Dakota 43. 14 states with 15 or more.
facts.unit: cents per bushel between the strongest and weakest state median
facts.source: AGSIST elevator network, state median basis (scripts/basis_method.py, data/basis-states.json)
